families.decision: Plain wild seafood, with species and harvest origin named.
buying_tips: Read wild-caught, the species and harvest origin on the label.
Look for a named fishing boat or small fishery on the pack.
Read the ingredients: seafood alone, with optional salt.
Pick sealed frozen packs or firm fish displayed on ice.

families.decision: Wild trout first; farmed rainbow trout with water, feed and farm details.
buying_tips: Look for wild-caught trout with harvest waters named.
Check farmed rainbow trout for a farm name and spring-fed wording.
Ask at the fish counter for the farm's water, feed and treatment records.
Skip trout labeled color added.

families.decision: Named wild fish, plain or in water or olive oil, with a short ingredient list.
buying_tips: Read the fish species and origin on the tin.
Read fish alone, or fish with water or olive oil and optional salt.
Skip tins listing soy oil, sunflower oil or hydrolyzed protein.
Check for an intact tin with no bulging, leaks or damaged seams.

families.decision: Named wild crab or lobster, moving when live or plainly cooked or frozen.
buying_tips: Read the species and harvest origin on the tag.
Look for a named fisher or small fishery on the label.
Check live animals for moving legs or claws.
Read raw or cooked on chilled or frozen portions.

families.decision: Live clams, mussels or oysters with a harvest tag and intact shells.
buying_tips: Look for a named grower or harvester on the sack tag.
Read the harvest waters and harvest date on the tag.
Check oysters, mussels and hard-shell clams for intact shells that close when tapped.
Ask at the fish counter to see the harvest tag for loose shellfish.

families.decision: Dayboat scallops with harvest details, scallops-only ingredients and no soaking.
buying_tips: Look for dayboat scallops with harvest area and date on the pack.
Read scallops as the only ingredient; skip added water or phosphates.
Ask at the fish counter to see the original tub and confirm no soaking.
Pick sealed frozen dayboat scallops when fresh dayboat catch is absent.

families.decision: Wild seafood from a named fishery, with the curing method and ingredients shown.
buying_tips: Read the species, wild-caught wording and harvest origin.
Look for a named small fishery or curer on the pack.
Check the curing method and storage directions on the label.
Pick intact packs kept chilled or frozen as their label directs.

salmon_wild_vs_farmed.decision: Wild Alaskan salmon, fresh or frozen, with the species named.
salmon_wild_vs_farmed.delta: Alaskan fresh season, May-Oct; sockeye and coho are named Pacific salmon species.

shrimp_imported_vs_domestic.decision: Wild American shrimp with species and harvest waters named.
shrimp_imported_vs_domestic.delta: Gulf white, pink or brown shrimp.

mercury_by_fish.decision: Wild sardines or salmon with the species named on the label.
mercury_by_fish.delta: Skip swordfish, shark, king mackerel and bigeye tuna.

canned_fish_choosing.decision: Plain wild sardines or Alaskan salmon, with skin and bones retained.
canned_fish_choosing.delta: Sardines and canned salmon with edible bones; skip skinless, boneless versions.

farmed_fish_by_species.decision: Farmed clams, mussels or oysters from a named grower, with a harvest tag.
farmed_fish_by_species.delta: These bivalves feed on plankton in the growing water.

seafood_certifications.decision: Wild seafood with species, origin and the MSC blue fish label.
seafood_certifications.delta: MSC marks wild fisheries; ASC marks farmed seafood.

canned_tuna.decision: Wild skipjack tuna in its own juices, water or olive oil.
canned_tuna.delta: Skipjack named on the can; light names a color category, not a species.

white_fish.decision: Plain wild Pacific cod with Alaska origin on the label.
white_fish.delta: Pacific cod and sablefish are different species; black cod means sablefish.

crab.decision: Wild crab with species and origin named, live and moving or plainly cooked.
crab.delta: Real crab meat; skip imitation crab or surimi.

lobster.decision: Live wild lobster with moving claws and a curling tail.
lobster.delta: New-shell Maine lobster is a summer and fall choice.

scallops.decision: Dayboat scallops, dry-packed, with scallops as the only ingredient.
scallops.delta: Maine inshore season, Dec-Apr; bay scallops are a different species from sea scallops.

clams_mussels_oysters.decision: Live clams, mussels or oysters from a named grower or harvester, with a harvest tag.
clams_mussels_oysters.delta: Littleneck hard clams are smaller than middlenecks and topnecks.

smoked_salmon.decision: Wild Alaskan salmon smoked over wood, with a short curing ingredient list.
smoked_salmon.delta: Natural wood smoke and salt, with optional organic sugar; skip liquid smoke or smoke flavoring.

seafood_counter.decision: Whole wild fish on ice, with clear eyes, shiny skin and intact fins.
seafood_counter.delta: Whole fish show the gills and eyes; skip sunken eyes or brown gills.

seafood_fish_roe.decision: Wild salmon roe with roe and salt as the only ingredients.
seafood_fish_roe.delta: Ikura means salmon roe; skip added dyes or taramasalata dip when buying plain roe.

seafood_fresh_sardines_mackerel.decision: Whole wild sardines or Atlantic mackerel on ice.
seafood_fresh_sardines_mackerel.delta: Atlantic or chub mackerel; skip king mackerel.

seafood_trout.decision: Whole wild trout, or rainbow trout from a named spring-fed small farm.
seafood_trout.delta: Whole trout with an intact snout and fins.

groups.title: Crab and lobster
groups.why_same: Both use species and harvest tags, named fishers, movement in live stock, and raw or cooked labels on portions.
